description: A litigation director must approve the company's strategy for seeking emergency injunctive relief against a competitor accused of using confidential software, including the scope of the requested injunction, forensic inspection, and customer-transition protections, with input from a senior associate and the client liaison.

shared_context.S1: The company alleges that a former employee took confidential software and that a competitor is now using it in a hosted product.
shared_context.S2: The competitor has denied wrongdoing and has refused to pause the hosted product voluntarily.
shared_context.S3: A preliminary-injunction hearing is scheduled in three weeks, and Marisol Vega must approve the response strategy before the motion papers are finalized.
shared_context.S4: At the weekly case-strategy meeting, Marisol asks litigation and client teams to report any material evidence, business constraints, or proposed filing commitments before she approves the strategy.

PF1.text: While reviewing a forensic image delivered after the strategy-memo cutoff, Ethan found the former employee's signed confidentiality agreement and logs showing that 4,800 files, including source code and deployment scripts, were copied to an external drive; the supplemental findings have not yet been added to the motion outline.

PF2.text: In this week's client call, Nadia confirmed that the client will support an injunction only if it permits a 30-day customer-transition period for existing hosted customers and does not shut down the customer-facing service during that period.

acceptance_conditions: The company must seek a preliminary injunction.
The requested injunction must cover both source code and deployment scripts.
The filing plan must request an expedited forensic inspection.
The injunction must allow a customer-transition period of exactly 30 days.
The customer-facing service must not be shut down during that 30-day period.
The supplemental forensic findings must be cited as justification for the strategy.

decisive_facts.why: The signed confidentiality agreement and evidence of 4,800 copied files change the strategy from relying on an uncorroborated allegation to seeking an injunction covering source code and deployment scripts, an expedited forensic inspection, and a supplemental-evidence filing.

The client's confirmed operating constraint changes the customer remedy from an unspecified injunction to an exact 30-day transition carveout with no shutdown of the customer-facing service during that period.
